props.lede: You know the part of Hey Jude where everyone starts singing. A Beatles sing-along is a playful hour of that. Two musicians play and lead the singing, and by the second song that’s your whole crowd.

headingText.html: It books for a fiftieth anniversary or an eightieth birthday, a company picnic or holiday party, a wedding welcome party, a school or library program, and an afternoon at a senior living community. Every crowd in that list already knows these songs.

THE ONE READER: whoever wants the whole crowd singing. Daniel's
     correction, 2026-09-24, after a pass that wrote the page to the senior
     living activity director: "this is WAY too focused on senior living.
     that is ONE potential client ... it excludes so many other booking
     possibilities." His brief: kids through seniors, marketed into senior
     living among other places but not only there. So the reader is defined
     by the desire, not the institution; the hero speaks to that desire, the
     second paragraph names the breadth once, and the occasions section
     gives each buyer a row of their own: family parties, company events,
     weddings, community events, senior living.

     Fourth pass, 2026-09-24, against the fifteen copywriting rules drafted
     in this session (in chat, pending Daniel's ratification, not yet global).

     Fifth pass, 2026-09-24, on Daniel's ruling: "the focus on booklets is
     an ops detail that needs mentioned only in faq. it's not a feature of
     the act. similarly decibel levels in numbers is a misread of the
     audience." The feature is two musicians getting a whole crowd singing;
     the booklets are how, and how lives in the FAQ with the footprint, the
     outlet, the arrival time, the paperwork and the standing date. The
     "How it runs" and "Booking it" sections are gone (the sitewide close
     already asks for the date and the venue). "Multi-instrumental" left
     the caption because with no instrument named it tells a buyer nothing;
     it stays in the repo note as his fact.

     Named act, spec'd presentation: the name publishes and no musician does
     (Daniel, 2026-09-22: "publish under the act name. no additional names").
     Act-hero shape, the same one Firstwater uses, with the style as the
     eyebrow and the name as the h1.

     Rewritten 2026-09-24 in the copy critique Daniel asked for. The first
     version said the same five facts in every section (booklets fourteen
     times, the duo twenty-three times), listed venues in four paragraphs,
     and put the site's own taxonomy on the page ("a named act", "books as
     one duo"). The identity section that restated it is gone.

     The lede was rewritten a second time the same day, after Daniel read the
     first rewrite's opener ("Two musicians play the Beatles and hand out
     lyric booklets, and everyone sings, from the grandchildren to the

rows.text: An anniversary, a milestone birthday, a retirement send-off or a backyard party, at the house or at a rented space. Whoever the party is for grew up on these records, and their grandchildren end up singing them too.
A summer picnic, the holiday party or the last night of a retreat. It’s the one thing the whole company does together, and it plays at a volume the tables can still talk across.
A welcome party, a rehearsal dinner or the after-party. The two families meet for the first time that weekend, and they all know these songs, so it’s the first thing they do together.

A library’s summer program, a school’s family night, a church picnic, a block party or a farmers market. It’s open to whoever walks up, so the audience is every age at once, and this is one of the few programs that works for the toddlers and the retirees in the same hour.
The residents know every one of these songs from the first time around. In memory care the same duo plays a shorter, quieter set to a smaller group.

props.html: The operational questions, from substitutions to decibel caps, are on the full question list.

items.q: What is Your Bird Can Sing?
items.a: A Beatles sing-along led by two musicians, booked through Signet Artists in Denver, for family parties, company events, weddings, community programs and senior living.

items.q: Is this a Beatles tribute band?
items.a: No. Two musicians play the Beatles songbook as themselves and lead the audience through the songs.

items.q: Does anyone need to know the words?
items.a: No. Everyone gets a lyric booklet and the duo leads the melody, so anyone who wants to sing can, and anyone who would rather sit and listen is welcome to.
One set of 45 to 60 minutes, or two shorter sets with a break. Requests are welcome.

items.q: What do we need to have ready?
items.a: About 8 by 6 feet of floor and one standard outlet. The duo brings sound support that's the right size for the venue, so you don't need a system of your own, and the musicians arrive about an hour before the start. Outdoors it needs shade over the musicians and an outlet within reach, and what happens if it rains is on the technical page.

About as loud as a conversation. People at the back hear the melody and the front table can keep talking. The duo sets the volume to the space and the crowd, so in a small space it plays with no amplification at all, and in a courtyard it plays louder to reach the back.

items.q: Can we book it every month?
items.a: Yes. It books as a standing date, the same afternoon each month or every other week, on one contract with one personal contact for the whole run, and the set changes from visit to visit.

items.q: Do you have a certificate of insurance and a W-9?
items.a: Yes. Both come in the same email as the contract, with an invoice that matches your purchase order, so a business office can set the vendor up before the date.

props._notes:
The FAQ is where the ops live, on Daniel's ruling of 2026-09-24: the
     booklets, the set length, the floor space and the outlet, the sound,
     the volume in words rather than decibels, the standing date, outdoors,
     and the paperwork. None of it is on the page above, because none of it
     is a feature of the act. The definition is first for the entity, and
     the tribute question is second on purpose: "beatles tribute band
     denver" is the strongest local query in this family and the answer is
     no, so the page says no where a reader will find it.
